title: indigo_docs: rewrite the scheduler guide for readability
description:
Owner request (2026-11-21): indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (about 15,000 words) is hard to read: the language is heavy, sentences pack a rule, its exceptions and cross-references together, and some passages are ambiguous. Rewrite it for readability without losing correctness.
Proposed structure (to be settled in the design stage): a short quick start (load the agents, upload one task, start, watch the plan); concepts in plain words (tasks and headers, constraints, priority, COMPACT vs VISIBILITY, hooks, meridian flips, where the data goes); a reference part with the exact rules, edge cases and property/setting tables. Style: short sentences, one idea per sentence, examples before rules, no mid-sentence cross-references, consistent terms, no ambiguity. Keep the existing worked examples and the 'Two nights compared' charts (indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE/*.png). Owner decisions that apply: no particular INDIGO GUI clients are named, indigo_prop_tool is used for examples; VISIBILITY uses priority only to choose which tasks get into the plan, COMPACT runs tasks in priority order (separate ticket fixes these first).
Design stage: propose the new outline and rewrite one section as a style sample for the owner's approval before the whole guide is rewritten. Every rule kept must be checked against the scheduler code (indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/). Review: correctness against the code and a separate fresh-eyes readability review. Keep links into the guide working (anchors used by SCHEDULER.md, PROPERTIES.md or other docs). No README.md changes.

outcome.summary:
Readability review (fresh eyes, amateur user who has never used the scheduler). Overall the guide reads well: short sentences, examples first, consistent structure, and the quick start leads to a running scheduler. Design 5.2 fixed questions all answered from the concepts part: high after normal (L370-371, L1424); when RESUME runs (L483, L540); where hook frames go (L665); urgent arrival (L699-706); stop a run at 02:00 (L235-259). COMPACT vs VISIBILITY and priority under each (L360-372) are clear. One blocking finding, the rest minor.

BLOCKING
B1. The meridian flip, OFFSET and VISIBILITY_FLIP_PENALTY are used before they are explained, and OFFSET is never explained in the concepts part. L392 "With the flip enabled at `OFFSET` 0 and the default penalty, Soul, Pleiades and Jellyfish start just after the meridian, and no run flips", L407 and the whole Two nights section (flip columns, L428-448) come before Meridian flips (L616-628). L620 shows `enable_meridian_flip(true, 0)` but never says what the second argument (OFFSET) means. L622 "flips when the hour angle of its target reaches `OFFSET` hours before the run ends" parses two ways ("OFFSET hours before the end"?); L1000 has the same wording. Fix: (a) at the start of Two nights (or end of Choosing a strategy) add: "A German equatorial mount must flip when a run crosses the meridian. Under `VISIBILITY`, `VISIBILITY_FLIP_PENALTY` makes the planner count each flip as lost imaging time, so it moves short runs to one side of the meridian. `COMPACT` ignores the penalty. `OFFSET` 0 means the mount flips at the meridian. See also: [Meridian flips](#meridian-flips)." (b) At L620 add: "The second argument of `enable_meridian_flip()` is `OFFSET`, in hours of hour angle. With 0 the mount flips at the meridian. A positive value flips that many hours later." The banned terms are gone. Round 1 B1 and M1-M20 are all resolved.
